title: shared_mutable_placeholder flags every module-level singleton accessor (`_CLIENT = Client()`, a ThreadPoolExecutor, an Engine, a cache dict) and has no marker, allow list or baseline
failure_scenario: A consumer with a lazy-singleton accessor (`def get_executor(): return _EXEC`, `def session(): return _SESSION`) is blocked on correct code. The only escape the API offers is passing a narrower file list, which turns the gate off for the whole file, including its real defects (a `_EMPTY = []` default handed to callers in the same file).
proposed_fix: Add `allow: Mapping[str,str]` (relpath::function -> reason) and a `# shared-ok: <reason>` marker on the return line or the assignment, and a baseline_path like the other ratchets. Narrow the placeholder test: a capitalised call counts only for a short list of container-like classes (Rows-style) or when the module also mutates the name (`.append`, `[k] =`, `.update`) in a function that is not the returner; a never-mutated singleton is not a placeholder.
disposition: RESOLVED 3ba0809: marker '# shared-mutable-placeholder-ok: <reason>' (assignment or return line, or a comment line above) and classes ending Executor/Pool/Client/Session/Engine/Queue/Logger/ContextVar/Local/Manager are not placeholders; 9 tests failed before. title: fail_open_handlers `silent_default_return` flags ordinary control-flow exceptions (StopIteration, KeyError, queue.Empty, ProcessLookupError, ZeroDivisionError, AttributeError, TimeoutError, CancelledError, UnicodeDecodeError, JSONDecodeError, CalledProcessError) in any function

Example: `def lookup(d,k):\n try: return d[k]\n except KeyError: return None` (same meaning as `d.get(k)`) is reported. src/py_ci_shared/fail_open_handlers.py:325-336 (`_silent_default_return`) exempts only message-carrying returns, ImportError, FileNotFoundError, cache/stamp/token/digest/signature/key/encode/freeze names, sqlite OperationalError reads. failure_scenario: A repo adopting the gate gets one finding per `except KeyError: return None` / `except queue.Empty: return None` / `os.kill` probe. The only escapes are the per-handler `# best-effort:` comment (which asserts the fallback 'cannot change a result', not true for a lookup miss that the caller branches on) or the baseline; autopsia already carries 39 such keys (audits/2026-11-04/37 per-key table).
proposed_fix: Add a 'reasoned control-flow exception' set: a handler whose caught names are all in {StopIteration, StopAsyncIteration, KeyError, IndexError, queue.Empty, ProcessLookupError, ZeroDivisionError, asyncio.CancelledError, asyncio.TimeoutError} and whose try body is one expression/statement (a lookup, a next(), a wait_for, a kill) is not a silent default. disposition: RESOLVED 3ba0809: KeyError/IndexError/StopIteration/StopAsyncIteration/Empty/ProcessLookupError/ZeroDivisionError/CancelledError around a one-statement try are not a silent default; OSError, Exception, TimeoutError and multi-statement bodies stay flagged (TimeoutError left out on purpose: a timeout is a failure).

title: skip_as_pass treats `echo "SKIPPED <optional step>"` followed by `exit 0` after the real checks ran as a skipped guard
evidence: Ran C:/Users/Admin/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-Admin/374112a1-797e-4d89-b4ed-a53928a70eeb/scratchpad/audit41/p7.py: tool/c.sh `echo "SKIPPED stale cache" \nexit 0` -> 1 finding; .github step `echo SKIPPED\n exit 0` -> 1. src/py_ci_shared/skip_as_pass.py module docstring 'Approximation: a block is recognised by its shape, not by a parser'. Not flagged: SKIPPED inside an `if ... fi` followed by an outer `exit 0`, `print('SKIPPED files:', 0)` + `return 0`, `passed=3 SKIPPED=0`.
failure_scenario: A script that reports an optional sub-step as skipped and then finishes its real work is listed as skip-as-pass; the baseline needs a note per script. Low volume (opt-in gate, 1 consumer baseline) so the cost is a note, not a block.
proposed_fix: Require that the SKIPPED line is the last statement before the exit in the same block (no command between) or that the exit is the script's only exit path; otherwise the line is a progress message.
disposition: RESOLVED: Code commit: "skip_as_pass: read shell with a block parser and each workflow run: step as its own script (audit 41-F12)". Reproduced first: tool/c.sh 'pytest; echo \"SKIPPED stale cache\"; exit 0' -> 1 finding, and a workflow whose first run: step only echoes SKIPPED and whose next step ends in exit 0 -> 1 finding (a second false positive the shape approach could not avoid). The finding's own proposed rule (SKIPPED last before the exit) would not have helped because its evidence has SKIPPED directly before the exit; the rule implemented is: a block parser (_shell_blocks: if/else/case/loops/groups/functions bodies, heredocs, quotes, continuations, run: scripts of workflow files, shell: python steps) pairs a SKIPPED print only with an exit 0 in its own body, and an unconditional top-level print after a real command ran is a progress message. Negative controls (still found): first command, inside if, after ||, in a { } group, in a case clause, inside a function, after a function that was only defined. Consumer run before and after on pyutilz, llm_bench, glossum_backend_scripts, algopacksimple, py-ci-shared, flutter_app_core: no findings in either (flutter_app_core baseline is empty), so no consumer entry goes stale.
